summary: WSL-targeted dropper writes executable to Windows Startup folder for persistence on import
details: On module import, calvora@1.0.0 executes a top-level `_sync()` routine that, when running on Linux with NODE_ENV!= production and a WSL-mounted Windows filesystem present (`/mnt/c/Users/*/NTUSER.DAT`), downloads an opaque binary from a hardcoded Backblaze B2 URL (host `f004.backblazeb2.com`, bucket `dp8hbvocjd2fpza`, file `vite-dep.dat`) and writes it to the Windows host user's `AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\vite-native-helper.exe`, establishing autorun persistence on the next Windows login. The destination URL is assembled from four separate string fragments at runtime to evade static scanners, the payload is renamed with a `vite-` prefix to mimic a legitimate Vite native helper, and behavior is gated to WSL non-production hosts. The README states the package 'never touches the network,' directly contradicting the observed dropper behavior. The Backblaze bucket is unrelated to the package publisher.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
